context: Round 3 builds Squire's set-up: from the download to the Squire's first reply, without Terminal, on a Squire owner's own Mac and under their own Claude sign-in. Three facts shape it. A fresh Mac has no usable Python until Apple's command line tools are installed (/usr/bin/python3 is then Apple's stub, which offers to install the tools rather than run Python), yet the Mac check and an unsupported Mac's refusal must run before anything changes. The plan is readable only through Claude Code after it is installed and signed in, which is itself a change to the Mac, so the plan check cannot come first. And the download is not signed by Apple, so macOS stops it once until the owner clicks Open Anyway in System Settings. Runtime facts below come from the documentation pages named (code.claude.com: setup, cli-reference, authentication, model-config, settings-reference, managed-settings, remote-control; support.apple.com/en-us/102445 for Gatekeeper; the man pages for launchd.plist, launchctl, codesign, xattr and sw_vers on macOS 26.3.1), from round 2's measured facts (ADR-003), from the probes run on a test user's Mac with Claude Code 2.1.319 on 2026-11-09 (each marked measured where it settles a fact), or are marked owed with the probe that settles them. Anything not stated outright by a source is marked inferred.
decision:
1. The download and its entry point. Squire's download is one per-user app, Squire.app, bundle identifier com.stravica.squire, that carries core: its own executable Contents/MacOS/Squire is the entry point, Contents/Info.plist names it, and Contents/Resources/core is core as released. In this repository the app's source is installer/Squire.app (its executable and Info.plist); the release puts core at Contents/Resources/core (the signed release bundle is round 4's), and a test world assembles the app the same way, a copy of installer/Squire.app with a copy of core/ at Contents/Resources/core. The executable is a zsh script (#!/bin/zsh): a bare macOS 13 has zsh, osascript, plutil and curl, needs no compiler for it, and its functions take Code Nodes. Everything before Apple's tools are present runs in it (lines 6 to 10); everything after runs core's Python, /usr/bin/python3 -B Contents/Resources/core/tools/set-up.py, started by the executable only once Apple's tools answer. Nothing of Squire's is fetched: Claude Code comes from its maker's installer and Apple's tools from Apple's own dialog. The app writes nothing inside itself.
2. Where set-up keeps things. The Squire home is SQUIRE_HOME when set, else ~/Library/Application Support/Squire, as core already reads it. Set-up's own record is set-up.json in the Squire home (line 13). Claude Code's config folder for Squire's session is claude-config in the Squire home (ADR-003 line 3); the sign-in goes there. The owner's folder is ~/Squire, and round 3 offers no other place (a choice of folder is a later round's candidate); it is never under Desktop, Documents, Downloads or iCloud Drive (macOS asks the owner before an app reads Desktop, Documents and Downloads: support.apple.com Mac help "Control access to files and folders on Mac"). A ~/Squire that is already a file, that resolves (its real path, links followed) into Desktop, Documents, Downloads or iCloud Drive, or that set-up cannot write, pauses set-up on "Squire: set-up paused" naming it, and is never removed, replaced or written; an owner's squire.json there that does not parse pauses set-up naming it, and is left byte for byte. The Squire home's squire.json, Squire's own config, holds ownerFolder, keychain (the login keychain, the production keychain from round 1) and backupFolder. The owner's squire.json, the file of that name at the top of the owner's folder, holds squireName and personality, where the runner already reads squireName (ADR-003 line 7), keeping any other keys it holds; once written it is the one authority for both, and no other copy is read.
3. The Mac's own commands, and how a test world reaches them. Set-up and the health check run the Mac's own commands (sw_vers, sysctl, id, xcode-select, curl, bash, osascript, open, plutil and every other) only from the system folders /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin and /sbin, each by its full path; the PATH the app is opened with is never consulted. When SQUIRE_SYSTEM_ROOT is set and names an existing absolute folder, those four folders are read under it instead (<root>/usr/bin and so on), Python included (<root>/usr/bin/python3); any other value is refused before any write on "Squire: cannot set up". claude is only ever found at the fixed places in ADR-003 line 5, never by PATH. Every subprocess set-up and the health check start (curl, bash with Claude Code's installer, claude --version, claude auth login, status and logout, osascript, open and the rest) runs in an environment built from nothing, as the runner's (ADR-003 line 4): HOME, USER, LOGNAME, a UTF-8 LANG, TMPDIR, PATH set to the four system folders (under the root when it is set) and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR where a claude call needs it, nothing inherited beyond these, never ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN; stdin from /dev/null; each call bounded (the download at 10 minutes and the sign-in at 15, lines 8 and 9; the health check's claude auth status at 30 seconds). A test world sets SQUIRE_SYSTEM_ROOT to its own system/ folder, which mirrors the four system folders: at the system path of each command the world fakes stands its fake (usr/bin/sw_vers, usr/sbin/sysctl, usr/bin/id, usr/bin/xcode-select, usr/bin/curl, usr/bin/osascript, usr/bin/open), and every other entry of the four real folders is a link to the real one, usr/bin/python3 to the Python the tests run, so the world reaches the Mac's real commands only through that one seam. The Mac check reads a fake sw_vers, a fake memory reading (sysctl -n hw.memsize), a fake group list (id -Gn) and a fake xcode-select; the download reads a fake curl that serves a fake Claude Code installer; the owner's answers come from a fake osascript that answers each window by its title; the browser is a fake open that records what it was asked to open. The world opens the app with a PATH of its own, whose first folder a test may fill with hostile commands of the same names; set-up never calls them. That answer source exists only in the test world; Squire ships no answer file and no switch for one.
4. Set-up's own windows. Each is an osascript dialog (display dialog, or choose from list for the plan), its title one of: "Squire: your Claude plan" (the declaration), "Squire: set up" (the one yes; buttons "Not now" and "Install"), "Squire: name your Squire" and "Squire: your Squire's personality" (each a default answer), "Squire: your plan" (the ask of line 9; buttons "Stop" and "Continue"), "Squire: your phone" (buttons "Later" and "Done"), "Squire: cannot set up" (a refusal before any change), "Squire: set-up stopped" (a stop after a change, and what was undone), "Squire: set-up paused" (a failure that leaves set-up to resume: what went wrong and to open Squire again) and "Squire: ready" (the end). Answers are read from osascript's own result: "button returned:<button>", with ", text returned:<text>" after a default answer; the chosen item for a list, or false when cancelled. Set-up never opens Terminal and never asks the owner to open anything but its own windows, the browser, System Settings and Apple's tools dialog; the Claude app is offered on the phone window, never required. On the Mac the owner talks to Squire at claude.ai/code in the default browser.
5. The steps, in order (readiness item 14's ten, in item 3's order), each with its id in the record: yes (the Mac check, the plan the owner declares and the one yes); claudeCode (Claude Code found or installed); signIn (the sign-in into Squire's config folder, then the plan read); appleTools; naming (the Squire's name and personality); ownerFolder; layDown (core laid down from the app's own core: the session and the wake-ups); backup (the nightly backup job); health (the health check); phone (optional); firstConversation. Item 14's second step, Claude Code and the sign-in, is recorded as two, claudeCode and signIn, so a sign-in that fails keeps Claude Code. The browser and voice-note steps are round 6's.
6. The Mac check, at every start of the app and before any write: macOS 13 or later (sw_vers -productVersion), 4 GB of memory or more (sysctl -n hw.memsize, 4294967296 bytes), both Claude Code's own floor (setup page, System requirements); and Apple's command line tools present (xcode-select -p exits 0 naming a folder that exists) or installable by this user, which is an administrator (admin among id -Gn). Versions compare as numbers, part by part. A fact the check cannot read is refused before any write on "Squire: cannot set up", naming what could not be read and the way on, never asked and never assumed: sw_vers missing, failing or printing no version; the memory reading missing, failing or not a whole number; the group list failing when Apple's tools are absent. A Mac that fails is refused before any write, on the "Squire: cannot set up" window, which names what is missing and the way on: an older macOS names macOS 13 and says to update macOS in System Settings; too little memory names 4 GB; a user who cannot install Apple's tools names Apple's command line tools and says to ask whoever administers this Mac to install them, or to set Squire up from an administrator's account. Each refusal leaves the home folder and every record exactly as found.
7. The declaration and the one yes, still before any write. The "Squire: your Claude plan" window lists Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise, Free, and I'm not sure. Free, or a cancelled window, is refused before any write on "Squire: cannot set up", naming Pro and the way on (a Pro plan or above at claude.ai, then open Squire again); I'm not sure goes on and the plan read decides (line 9). Then the one yes, "Squire: set up", names every piece set-up adds: Claude Code, with its own background updates (setup page, Auto-updates); Apple's command line tools, with the system's own administrator password prompt, when they are not already there; Squire itself; and each background job lay-down writes (the session runner, the wake-ups and the backup). Not now installs nothing, writes nothing and ends set-up. Install creates the Squire home and the record, and nothing outside the named list is ever installed.
8. Claude Code. Found when the fixed places of ADR-003 line 5 hold a claude, owned by the user and not writable by others, that answers claude --version (exit 0, a version: setup page, Verify your installation); then nothing is installed and it is never recorded as added. Otherwise set-up downloads the native installer with curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh, bounded at 10 minutes, into a file of its own in the Squire home, and only when curl exits 0 runs it with bash (setup page, Native Install: the launcher at ~/.local/bin/claude is a link into ~/.local/share/claude/versions/; inferred: no administrator). The places the native installer uses are ~/.local, ~/.local/bin, ~/.local/bin/claude, ~/.local/share, ~/.local/share/claude, ~/.local/share/claude/versions, ~/.local/state, ~/.local/state/claude, ~/.cache, ~/.cache/claude, ~/.claude and ~/.claude.json (measured: besides the launcher and the versions folder the native installer makes ~/.claude, ~/.claude.json, ~/.cache/claude and ~/.local/state/claude under HOME, and writes no shell file). Before downloading, set-up records claudeCode's entries in added, each {path, made, savedCopy}: every one of those places that does not exist, made "created"; and every pre-existing file among them that the installer changes (the launcher, and the files named here as measured to change), made "changed", with a saved copy of its bytes (a link as its target) taken inside the Squire home before the installer runs and named by savedCopy. Set-up lists every path under those places before the installer runs and again after it ends, and records every path that appeared as made "created". The undo (line 9) removes only what set-up created, newest first; restores what it changed byte for byte from its saved copy; and keeps anything inside a folder set-up created that set-up did not write: that folder stays, and "Squire: set-up stopped" names it. Every pre-existing byte survives the undo, a pre-existing set-up record included. An undo step that fails (claude auth logout, a removal, a restore), or a pre-existing file whose bytes changed with no saved copy, is named on "Squire: set-up stopped" and stays in added, and that window never says the Mac is as set-up found it. Measured over a home that already held a partial install (2.1.319, 2026-11-09, run from a launchd job with no terminal): the native installer rewrote a pre-existing ~/.claude.json, keeping its keys and adding its own, and left a copy of the old file in ~/.claude/backups/; it re-pointed a pre-existing launcher link to the new version; it kept an incomplete older version entry and left every other pre-existing file unchanged. So ~/.claude.json and the launcher are the files set-up saves before the installer runs, and the installer's backup copy is a path that appeared. A path it makes outside these places is a limit, none seen on that run. A download that fails, times out or is cut short runs no installer, leaves no launcher, records nothing done, and shows "Squire: set-up paused" naming the download and to open Squire again; the next run starts the step again from its start. Measured: run from a launchd job in the login session, with no terminal and no TTY, the documented command completed in 24 to 35 seconds, asked nothing, needed no administrator and opened no window; claude --version then printed "2.1.319 (Claude Code)". The real app runs with the owner's own HOME, where the probe used a folder of its own.
9. The sign-in and the plan read. Set-up runs claude auth login with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to Squire's config folder (cli-reference: claude auth login), in the environment line 3 builds, which opens the browser's sign-in page (measured on 2026-11-09 by the owner's own run on a test Mac: from a launchd job in the login session with no terminal and no TTY, the sign-in page opened in the browser, auth login exited 0 once the owner signed in there, and the fresh config folder read signed in); the sign-in is bounded at 15 minutes. Signed in means claude auth status in that folder exits 0 and the folder's .claude.json holds oauthAccount; loggedIn is read and recorded but not required (a wrong reading is caught when the health check next pauses on the sign-in) (ADR-003 line 3). A sign-in that is cancelled, times out or has no internet is explained on "Squire: set-up paused" (the sign-in, and to open Squire again), keeps everything done before it, and the next run resumes at the sign-in with Claude Code kept. Then the plan read, from claude auth status in that folder: its subscriptionType field. Measured: 2.1.319 prints subscriptionType (a lower-case plan word, "max" on the one account seen) and planTier ("max_20x") beside the documented loggedIn, authMethod and configDirectory; neither is documented, so only the one value was seen. pro, max, ultra, team and enterprise go on (setup page: Claude Code needs a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise or Console account). free is below Pro. A value set-up does not know, a missing field, or an answer it cannot read is asked on "Squire: your plan": "Squire could not confirm your plan; it needs Pro or above. Continue?"; Continue goes on and is recorded as consent in set-up's approvals ledger (line 13), Stop is treated as below Pro. A plan below Pro stops set-up and undoes what set-up added (line 8): claude auth logout in Squire's config folder (cli-reference), then each entry in added, newest first, removing what set-up created and restoring what it changed, never touching a Claude Code or any byte that was there before; "Squire: set-up stopped" names Pro and the way on, and says the home folder is as set-up found it only when every undo step succeeded. The plan read comes before Apple's tools and everything else system-wide, so the undo never needs an administrator.
10. Apple's command line tools. Present only when xcode-select -p exits 0 naming a folder that exists: the one test at the Mac check (line 6), during the wait and at the end-state check (line 13); then nothing is installed. Otherwise xcode-select --install opens Apple's own dialog and set-up waits for that test to pass, looking every 10 seconds and at most 60 minutes. Tools not confirmed in that time are not recorded done; "Squire: set-up paused" says Apple's tools are not finished and to open Squire again, and the next run starts this step again from its start (that a script can start Apple's tools dialog is owed to the release Verify's from-zero run, TM3). Then the executable starts core's Python steps.
11. Naming, the owner's folder and lay-down. naming asks "Squire: name your Squire" and "Squire: your Squire's personality" (line 15 bounds the answers) and keeps both answers, trimmed, in set-up.json (squireName, personality) until ownerFolder writes them to the owner's squire.json, which then removes them from set-up.json. ownerFolder makes ~/Squire when absent (line 2 names when it pauses instead), writes ownerFolder into the Squire home's squire.json and squireName and personality into the owner's squire.json; a folder already there is kept as it is, and an owner's squire.json already there keeps its other keys. Before lay-down, set-up copies the app's core (Contents/Resources/core) into the Squire home's release folder, release/core, and checks the copy against the app's by digest, file by file; release in set-up.json names that folder, and every later lay-down, set-up's and the known fixes' (line 17), reads from there and never from the app, which the owner may move or delete. layDown runs lay-down, /usr/bin/python3 -B <Squire home>/release/core/tools/lay-down.py <Squire home>/release/core, which lays core down, writes the config folder's settings and Squire's launchd agents and loads them only in the account's own home (ADR-003 line 2).
12. The first conversation, and why a server stopped. firstConversation waits, at most 2 minutes, for the session: one session record whose process is alive and listens on its socket (ADR-003 lines 10 and 18), then opens https://claude.ai/code in the default browser (open) and shows "Squire: ready" naming the Squire. When the server stops before any session, the runner records the server's own last line in runner.json's problems ("no session: Claude Code's Remote Control server stopped before any session started: " then that line; round 2's TEST saw "Unable to determine your organization for Remote Control eligibility" on 12 of 12 starts with runner.json empty and the health check silent); set-up's last step names it on "Squire: set-up paused" and records nothing done, and the health check names it as a fault only once a session has run. The guide for the first conversation (what Squire can do, how approval works, the privacy words, house style, fresh starts) is in the instructions lay-down writes (line 15); the reply that names the Squire is the Journey test's.
13. The record, each step's end state, the lock and the re-run. set-up.json in the Squire home is {"done": [the step ids done, in order], "added": [{"path", "made": "created" or "changed", "savedCopy" (changed only)}], "release": <the Squire home's release folder>, "declared": <the plan the owner declared>, "squireName", "personality"}, the last two only until ownerFolder writes them to the owner's squire.json, written whole through a file beside it and a rename. Consent (the one yes, and Continue on a plan set-up cannot confirm) is recorded with its time in an append-only approvals ledger of set-up's own in the Squire home and re-confirmed from there at every run, never from done; the declaration is kept in the record and not asked again once the yes is confirmed. A set-up.json that does not parse, holds wrong types, holds unknown, duplicate, out-of-order or gapped step ids, is truncated, or sits beside a leftover neighbour file fails closed to running again from the start (the declaration and the one yes asked again); the bad file is set aside in the Squire home, never adopted and never deleted. A step whose result cannot be written to the record is not done, and set-up pauses. Every step checks its end state before it starts and after it ends, is safe to run again, and is recorded done only when its end state is seen after it ends: yes, the ledger holds the one yes; claudeCode, line 8's found test; signIn, line 9's signed-in test and a plan read that went on; appleTools, line 10's test; naming, both answers kept (in set-up.json, or in the owner's squire.json once ownerFolder has written them); ownerFolder, the folder exists, the Squire home's squire.json names it and the owner's squire.json holds squireName and personality; layDown, the release folder matches the app's core by digest, lay-down exited 0 and the installed core's digests match (ADR-003 line 6); backup, its agent loaded in the user's own launchd domain (gui/<uid>) wherever lay-down loads agents (the account's own home), and written elsewhere; health, the health check names none of the faults set-up's own steps lay down (the runner not running once the runner lay-down loaded has had up to 30 seconds to take its lock, a floor file changed, not signed in), and every other line it prints is shown as found on "Squire: ready"; set-up's last step names a server that stopped before any session (line 12), and the health check names it as a fault only once a session has run; phone, the owner answered; firstConversation, the browser was opened at claude.ai/code. A step whose end state cannot be confirmed (a launcher whose version folder is incomplete, Apple's tools still installing, a step killed part way) runs again from its start and is never counted done. One set-up at a time: an advisory lock (flock) on a lock file in the Squire home, taken at start when the Squire home exists, otherwise the moment Install creates it and before any other write, held until the app exits and gone with its process; a second set-up, whatever its TMPDIR, exits at once on "Squire: cannot set up", saying Squire's set-up is already running. The runner's gate, as built: during the first set-up only, while set-up.json's done lacks phone and no session has been recorded in the Squire home, the runner holds its lock and starts no session; set-up opened again later never holds it (phone is the step id the runner reads; the meaning is the first set-up only, so a re-run of set-up that pauses never stops a working Squire). Running the app again resumes at the first step not recorded done; a step recorded done whose end state no longer holds runs again; over a finished set-up it repairs what no longer holds and keeps the owner's folder and squire.json's settings. When the sign-in is gone, running the app again resumes at the sign-in step, and the health check's line for it says to open Squire's installer to sign in again. Uninstall is out of round 3.
14. The compaction window. core/settings.json carries "autoCompactWindow": 500000 (model-config: the auto-compact window; settings-reference: 100000 to 1000000 or "auto" from 2.1.288), laid into the config folder by lay-down, which the runner checks equal to core's before every start (ADR-003 lines 3 and 6); set-up reaches it by calling lay-down. Nothing is written to the owner's ~/.claude, whose settings, shell environment and command line never reach Squire's session (ADR-003 lines 3, 4 and 7). Measured: a session reading Squire's config folder reported its window through Claude Code's own /context as 500k with the key and 1m without it, on the same model (claude-haiku-5-5, read through claude -p with that folder); the Remote Control session started as the runner starts it loaded the same settings.json (its SessionStart hook ran from it) and gives no remote report of its window. So the key is the route, and the runner's CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=500000, the pre-ruled fallback, is not built. The update keys (autoUpdatesChannel stable, a minimumVersion floor) live in core's settings when they are built, in round 4 with Claude Code's own updates; round 3 binds no test to them. The health check reads every source it knows and names any value other than 500000, with its source: core's installed settings and the config folder's settings, each at the top level and per model under modelSettings; the session's environment as the runner's agent sets it; the managed settings file and its managed-settings.d folder in /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode; and the com.anthropic.claudecode managed preferences domain in /Library/Managed Preferences (managed-settings page). A managed source that exists but cannot be read gives "cannot confirm the compaction window", naming the source; never a pass and never silence. So does any present source the health check cannot read or parse: malformed JSON in any settings source, a malformed plist, a folder it cannot list or traverse, a modelSettings entry that is not an object, a runner plist it cannot read; and so does a present source that could override the window and that the health check does not read, the per-user managed preferences file /Library/Managed Preferences/<user>/com.anthropic.claudecode.plist among them. Claude Code caps the window at the model's own context window (model-config). The health check learns which models run below 500k from core/model-windows.json, a list in core the builder writes from the model-config page, naming each such model and its window (documented: Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 run at 200K without their [1m] variant; Opus 4.7 and later, Sonnet 5 and later, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5 run with the 1M window by default). For a model on that list, a value at or above its window is not drift and no line names it; every other model is checked against 500000. The health check reads those system places under the root /, and under SQUIRE_SYSTEM_ROOT when that is set: the test world's own folder, the one way a test reaches a place only an administrator can write (a switch that exists for the tests, listed for the owner to strike).
15. The name and personality. squireName and personality live in the owner's squire.json at the top of the owner's folder: the owner's own file, which set-up writes from the owner's answers and the session changes only with the owner's yes (the floor's rule for the owner's folder). Lay-down writes them into CLAUDE.md in the config folder, which Claude Code loads as the user's own instructions for Squire's session, at every lay-down, and the runner writes it again before every start; both carry them unchanged. Lay-down's block in CLAUDE.md opens with the line <!-- squire persona --> and closes with the line <!-- end squire persona -->. Naming asks again, on the same window and saying why, for an empty or blank value, a name over 40 or a personality over 400 characters after trimming, control characters or newlines, either of that block's comment marks (<!-- and -->), a Markdown heading (a value that starts with #) or a code fence (``` or ~~~), and never stores such a value; values are stored trimmed, and the stored value reaches the owner's squire.json, CLAUDE.md and --name byte for byte. Measured: a CLAUDE.md in CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR loaded in a Remote Control session started as the runner starts it, listed in the session's own transcript as the user's instructions, and the session answered with the word only that file held. --name carries the stored squireName (ADR-003 line 7). In round 3, "after Squire is updated" reads "after core is laid down again": the bound test lays a changed core down and finds both unchanged in what the session loads; round 4 proves it again through the signed update.
16. The nightly backup. core/tools/backup.py, run by its own launchd agent, com.stravica.squire.backup, which lay-down writes beside the other two (/usr/bin/python3 -B with the installed copy, SQUIRE_HOME in its environment, StartCalendarInterval at 02:30 every night, no KeepAlive; loaded only in the account's own home). It backs the owner's folder (ownerFolder) up into backupFolder from squire.json: by default the iCloud Drive folder ~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Squire Backup; any folder in the test world. The backup holds current/, the owner's folder as it was at the last run, and archive/<UTC date and time of the run>/, one per run: a file removed from the owner's folder moves from current/ into that run's archive folder, and a changed file's earlier copy moves there before the new copy goes into current/; nothing in the backup is ever deleted or overwritten. The job creates backupFolder only when its parent exists, so with iCloud Drive off the destination is absent. A destination that is absent, not writable or full gives no partial pass: the job exits non-zero, records the run as failed in backup.json in the Squire home, and the health check prints a line naming the backup and the destination; the next night's run tries again in full, and a run that succeeds clears the line. A source entry the job cannot read, a special file (a socket, a device or a pipe), or a file that changes or vanishes during its copy is named by the health check on a line of its own, current/ keeps its last copy of it, and the rest is backed up; an owner's folder that is absent or cannot be read at run time is a failed run, recorded as failed, in which nothing moves into the archive. The backup step's end state is its agent loaded in the user's own launchd domain (line 13). Measured: a LaunchAgent's /usr/bin/python3 made, wrote, read back and removed a folder directly under the home (beside ~/Squire) with no prompt; it did the same in the iCloud Drive folder of a user with iCloud Drive on, with no prompt; that the copy then syncs was not observed (the probe file lived under a second). Real sync is a by-hand line of the Journey walk and the release Verify.
17. The known fixes, from the health check's own lines, each checked by the health check itself rather than read from the runner's last record: the runner not running (no runner holds its lock in the Squire home): reload Squire's agents, bootstrapping each agent lay-down wrote that is not loaded, only in the account's own home, as lay-down loads them (ADR-003 line 2); a floor file changed (an installed floor file differs from its digest): lay core down again from the Squire home's release folder (line 11); not signed in (claude auth status in the config folder does not answer signed in): open Squire's installer to sign in again, a fix the owner makes, which changes nothing by itself and for which nothing is asked; a moved settings file: named only, it is the owner's file, and no fix is offered. The floor keeps refusing a core change from inside the session, yes or no; there is no floor exception. For a fix that changes anything, the health check prints the fault's line and the request that asks for its fix, /usr/bin/python3 <Squire home>/core/tools/health.py --request runner or --request floor; the session makes that request, and the floor asks the owner for it through its ordinary ask (a block naming the one fault and its fix, with a request id); the owner's yes is recorded in the approvals ledger with that fault and its time. The request never runs in the session: after the yes it is still blocked, and that block leaves the yes unused. The outside job performs it: the wake-ups scheduler's existing 60-second run (/usr/bin/python3 -B core/tools/wake-up.py --due, from the agent lay-down already writes) reads the ledger on each tick and, only when it finds an approved, unused, fresh fix, runs the health check's perform step, health.py --perform, once; a tick with nothing pending costs one ledger read and performs nothing. The perform step consumes the yes atomically before it acts, and acts only when the yes is exact (its fault is still present), fresh (given less than 30 minutes before, by the time on the yes's answer record in the ledger) and unused: it runs the one fix the yes names (reload the agents; or lay core down again from the release folder, and when that folder is missing or unreadable it does not try and says to open Squire's installer), runs the check again, and writes its result where the health check prints it at its next run, one plain line: "fixed: <fault>", "still: <fault>" or "could not try: <fault>: <reason>". A stale, mismatched or already used yes changes nothing and gives the "could not try" line saying why. One yes covers one fault. A crash after the yes is consumed is reported at the next check as the fault still there, and is never replayed. Nothing is performed without a recorded yes. Signing in again before the sign-in ends: the health check reads when Squire's sign-in ends only from claude auth status in the config folder, its loginExpiresAt (measured: 2.1.319 prints it, an ISO 8601 time, beside loggedIn, from an environment built from nothing; undocumented; the token is never read), and names that day on a line of its own with the request /usr/bin/python3 <Squire home>/core/tools/health.py --request sign-in. Within seven days of that day the scheduler's tick fires one wake-up through Squire's own router (core/tools/wake-up.py) naming the day (its date, YYYY-MM-DD, in the Mac's local time) and the one action, signing in again, at most once a day. The act is the owner's yes to that request, recorded and consumed exactly as a fix's: the perform step then runs set-up's sign-in step from the Squire home's release folder, claude auth login with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set to Squire's config folder in the environment line 3 builds, which opens the browser's sign-in page with no Terminal (line 9, measured), and nothing else. A sign-in nobody renewed in time is caught as before: the health line says to open Squire's installer to sign in again, and running it again resumes at the sign-in (line 13). An end the health check cannot read gives no warning and changes nothing. The new health lines (the known fixes, the compaction window and the backup) are named for an installed Squire, one whose core is laid down in the Squire home; a Squire home with no core laid down is checked as rounds 1 and 2 left it. A fault not on the list (an ignored overlay, a server that stopped before any session, a backup that could not run) is named and nothing is offered. Round 3 prints lines; the page is round 6's and the ticket is round 4's.
18. The phone and the end. phone shows "Squire: your phone", how to install the Claude app on the phone and sign in to the same Claude account, and is done on either answer: set-up completes with no phone, and the phone can join later. Closing the laptop or quitting during the first conversation leaves every earlier step done; the session resumes under the same session id (ADR-003 line 11), so the conversation goes on where it stopped, and running the app again finishes the last step.
19. What the no-Terminal release check and the Journey test read on a target Mac, over SSH as the Squire owner's user. Each needs a target fresh at its own start and depends on no other test's run: it first asserts and records a fresh baseline (no Squire home, no owner's folder, no Claude Code under the target's home, no transcript in Squire's config folder) and fails, never passes, on a target that is not fresh. Every read honours one Squire home, the one the record read names. The window list: CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo through osascript -l JavaScript gives each on-screen window's owning process id, owner name and layer, with no permission held (titles are withheld without Screen Recording, and none is asked for); lsappinfo info -only bundleid <pid> gives the owning app's bundle identifier (measured). Application windows are layer 0. The no-Terminal check watches continuously: a watcher on the target reads the window list every 100 milliseconds for the whole run, across set-up and a repair re-run over the finished set-up, and records each new layer-0 window with its owner's bundle identifier and process ancestry. Every new layer-0 window must belong to the allow-list. A window whose owning process descends from Squire's app process is Squire's: set-up's own dialogs are drawn by osascript, which has no bundle identifier (owed: that a dialog's owner is the osascript process the app started, the first run of this check). Any other window's bundle identifier, compared without regard to case, must be the default browser (the https handler LaunchServices names, and Safari; with none named, Safari only), System Settings (com.apple.systempreferences), Gatekeeper's own message (com.apple.coreservices.uiagent), Apple's tools dialog (com.apple.dt.CommandLineTools.installondemand) or the Claude app (com.anthropic.claudefordesktop); any other app's window fails, and a window whose owner neither descends from Squire's app nor has a bundle identifier the check can read fails. The check fails unless it saw at least one real set-up window drawn by the Mac's own osascript: its answer source, laid under a SQUIRE_SYSTEM_ROOT of its own on the target (line 3), draws each set-up window through /usr/bin/osascript, closes it after two seconds and answers from the test world. A hidden terminal session with no window is inside the promise. Set-up's progress is read from set-up.json in the target's Squire home; the session from its record (ADR-003 line 18); the first reply from the session's own transcript in the config folder: the first assistant entry after the owner's first message sent after set-up finished, in that session. The backup step's agent is read loaded on the target (launchctl print gui/<uid>/com.stravica.squire.backup exits 0).
20. Defaults where the design leaves the call open: preferences, recorded with the design and bound to no test. The app and its processes: Info.plist carries the executable, the identifier, the name, the package type APPL, the version and LSMinimumSystemVersion 13.0; set-up.py takes one argument, the app's core folder, and backup.py none, each exiting 0 when its work finished and non-zero otherwise, the window shown being the owner's answer; every path is passed as its own argument, never through a shell string; the executable checks its own core at every start before any write and refuses a missing or unreadable one on "Squire: cannot set up" as a damaged download to fetch again; "Squire: set-up paused" names the step in plain words and the way on, with no path or raw output, the detail going to a log in the Squire home. The Mac check: 4294967296 bytes or more is eligible ("4 GB" is for display); only the whole word admin among id -Gn's words counts; every failing condition is named, in line 6's order. The lock: a lock no live process holds is free whatever its file says, and a lock that cannot be made is "Squire: cannot set up" naming the Squire home, never "already running". Window answers set-up cannot read: a non-zero exit or an unreadable result is the window's cautious answer and never a yes (the declaration a cancel, the one yes Not now, the plan ask and the naming windows a pause), with osascript's exit code kept in the log; a naming window closed after earlier steps pauses set-up with nothing undone, and is asked again next run; the phone step is done on any outcome. Files set-up writes: keys set-up does not set are kept, and over a finished set-up an existing ownerFolder, keychain and backupFolder are kept; set-up.json and its neighbour are 0600 and the Squire home 0700; CLAUDE.md is written through a neighbour file and a rename, 0600; the owner's values are kept, the file's formatting and key order not promised; an owner's squire.json unreadable at a refresh leaves CLAUDE.md as last written, with a health line naming the file. The download and Claude Code's installer: the installer is downloaded into the Squire home and removed after its run whatever the outcome, with curl -fsSL --max-time 600 to its own file; an empty body, or one whose first line is not a #! line, is a failed download, never run, and a pause; the installer's own run is bounded at 10 minutes too, past which its process group is killed and the step paused; an installer that exits non-zero leaves claudeCode not done and added kept for an undo; claude --version is bounded at 30 seconds, a timeout meaning not found, and a version answer is exit 0 with output starting digits.digits.digits. The sign-in and the plan read: the 15-minute bound kills auth login's whole process group and leaves the browser page; the paused window says timed out only when set-up's own clock ran out, otherwise that the sign-in did not finish, never matching stderr text; each of set-up's auth status calls is bounded at 30 seconds, a timeout being not signed in; signed in needs exit 0 and an object with loggedIn true; subscriptionType is trimmed and lower-cased, and a value that is not a string is unknown, so asked. Apple's tools: whatever xcode-select --install returns, set-up waits within line 10's bound; a re-run while Apple's dialog is open runs the step from its start; the step is done only when line 13's after-check answers too and /usr/bin/python3 -B -V answers; Apple's dialog is left alone when the bound passes. Lay-down and repair: layDown's end state also needs every plist lay-down writes present and parsing; a lay-down that fails part way is not done and runs whole next time; a repair runs only the steps whose end state no longer holds, and lay-down writes the persona from the owner's file whenever it runs. Health lines and fixes: the runner's grace ends when a runner holds its lock or 30 seconds pass, and a lock file that cannot be read is its own "cannot confirm the runner" line; one line per problem, exit 1 when there is any, drift and cannot-confirm each on its own line; a reload leaves loaded agents alone; whether a runner holds its lock is tested without waiting and released at once; each fault is its own line, and only a fix that changes something gets a request. The first conversation and the server's reason: a failed open of claude.ai/code pauses naming the browser and the address; the live-session test is the router's identity check (ADR-003 line 12), more than one live record waiting until there is one, and a session seen then lost is looked for again within the 2 minutes; the phone and first-conversation steps are not repeated over a finished set-up; the server's reason is its last non-blank line with terminal escapes removed (a last line without a newline counts), or "stopped before any session with no output" with its exit code, cut at 300 characters with control characters removed, kept on the Mac, added beside other problems, given only when no session record was written after that server started, and cleared when a session starts and passes the identity check. The backup's record, archive and failures: backup.json is {"lastRun": {"at", "result": "passed" or "failed", "destination", "reason"}}, each run replacing it; archive folders are archive/YYYY-MM-DDTHHMMSSZ in UTC, with -2 and -3 appended within one second, made only when something moves into them; bytes, mode bits and modification time are kept; links are copied as links, never followed; empty folders are kept; each file is copied to a temporary name and renamed, the run passing only when every file landed, so current/ never holds a torn file; a file already moved to the archive stays after a failure and the next run completes current/; temporary files are removed at the next run's start; a second backup at once exits non-zero with a log line; each run compares the whole owner's folder with current/ afresh; a missing, relative or non-string backupFolder, a destination inside the owner's folder or the Squire home, or a destination that is a file or a link is a failed run with a health line and nothing written; the real write decides "not writable", and "full" is said only on a no-space or quota error, otherwise "could not write"; a path that changes type moves its earlier copy, file or tree, to the archive whole first, and a removed folder moves there whole under its relative path; nothing is excluded, hidden files and the owner's squire.json included; folders are 0700, copied files keep their mode, and backup.json is 0600. The compaction sources: every regular *.json directly inside managed-settings.d counts, subfolders not followed; links among managed files are followed for reading, the line naming the path in the managed place; only the integer 500000 passes, so "auto" or any other present value is drift naming the value; one line per differing value, each naming its source and, per model, the model; the installed core's settings and the config folder's are the sources checked, and the repository is never read. Progress: no window beyond Apple's dialog and the browser shows progress in round 3; a window appears at each owner action.
consequences:
Usage model for the budgets and timeouts the criteria and steps carry; every figure is an assumption unless a source is named.
The 500k compaction window. Typical: a Squire owner's day is a few short conversations and wake-ups in one long session; the session compacts at 500k tokens and never grows into a 1M-token session, so each turn after a compaction costs at most about half what a full 1M context would (model-config: the window is capped at the model's own). Heavy: a long research job fills the window several times a day; each fill costs one compaction, and the health check names any setting that would lift the window. A model with a smaller context runs at its own window, which costs less.
The nightly backup. Typical: an owner's folder of a few thousand small files and a few hundred MB, a few dozen changed files a night; one run copies the changes in seconds to minutes. Heavy: a first run over tens of GB, or a night with thousands of changed files; the run takes as long as the copy, and missed nights (the Mac asleep at 02:30) are coalesced by launchd into one run on waking (man launchd.plist, StartCalendarInterval). The archive grows by every changed or removed file and is never pruned in round 3.
Set-up's timeouts. The download: typical seconds to a minute for Claude Code's installer and binary; heavy, a slow connection, bounded at 10 minutes, then paused to resume. The sign-in: typical one to two minutes in the browser; heavy, the owner steps away, bounded at 15 minutes, then paused to resume. Apple's tools: typical 5 to 15 minutes from Apple's dialog; heavy, a slow connection or a dialog left unanswered, bounded at 60 minutes, then paused to resume. The session at the last step: typical seconds (round 2's walk: the record 5 seconds after lay-down); heavy, a refused account or a slow first start, bounded at 2 minutes, then the server's reason or a pause.
Accepted residuals, written at round 3's open (none ships past the release Verify unruled): (a) between an approved settings write and the runner's stop, a tool call may run without the floor; (b) an approved program holding the session's messaging token could post a bare yes; (c) a write the floor cannot resolve, once allowed, can reach the approvals ledger; (d) a program that reaches /usr/bin/security indirectly after one yes can print a secret, accepted for v0.1. Also: the floor digests do not yet cover core/lib/squire.py, and a job with no record keeps no marks until its first mark.
SQUIRE_SYSTEM_ROOT (line 3): a program already running as the owner can set it in launchd's environment and so change the Mac check, the consent windows and the install source, the same class as the other routes that need code already running as the owner; no test is bound to it. Set-up honours it only when it names an existing absolute folder; any other value is refused on "Squire: cannot set up".
The Gatekeeper click (Open Anyway in System Settings, Privacy and Security, then Open: support.apple.com/en-us/102445) is a by-hand line of the Journey walk and the release Verify, never a bound assertion; that it is offered for an ad-hoc-signed, quarantined app whose executable is a zsh script on macOS 26, and that the app then runs with no Terminal window, is measured (the owner's own run on a test Mac, 2026-11-09; the stage-keeper's Open Anyway probe record). That the sign-in opens the browser from a job with no terminal and lands in Squire's config folder is measured (the owner's own run on a test Mac, 2026-11-09: auth login exited 0 with no TTY once the owner signed in on the page that opened, and the fresh config folder read signed in; the stage-keeper's sign-in probe record). Real iCloud, Apple's tools from a script (TM3) and a from-zero Mac are the release Verify's.

alternativesConsidered.name: An installer package (.pkg)
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship set-up as a package whose scripts run as root after an administrator password.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Every owner would need an administrator password, the scripts run as root outside the owner's login session where Squire's agents live, and the per-user pieces (Claude Code, the config folder, the agents) need no administrator.

alternativesConsidered.name: The app fetches core from a release asset
alternativesConsidered.summary: Download core at set-up instead of carrying it.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: It would depend on round 4's signed release and its checks before they exist; carrying core keeps round 3 to what is proven here.

alternativesConsidered.name: The first step in Swift
alternativesConsidered.summary: A Swift executable built for macOS 13 for the Mac check and the steps before Python.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: It needs a build step and a toolchain in the release, and its checks take Code Nodes only on a class or a binding; zsh, osascript, plutil and curl are already on a bare macOS 13.

alternativesConsidered.name: The first step in Python
alternativesConsidered.summary: Run core's Python from the start.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: On a fresh Mac /usr/bin/python3 is Apple's stub until Apple's tools are installed, so the Mac check and its refusal could not run before a change.

alternativesConsidered.name: Check the plan before anything changes
alternativesConsidered.summary: Refuse a plan below Pro before any change, as first worded.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The plan is readable only through Claude Code after it is installed and signed in; the owner's declaration stops before any change and the read after sign-in undoes what set-up added.

alternativesConsidered.name: Read the plan only after the sign-in
alternativesConsidered.summary: No declaration; only the read, with the undo.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: An owner who knows their plan is below Pro would see Claude Code installed and removed for nothing.

alternativesConsidered.name: Install Apple's tools before Claude Code
alternativesConsidered.summary: Apple's tools first, so Python runs the rest.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: They are system-wide and cannot be removed without an administrator, so a plan found below Pro afterwards could not leave the Mac as set-up found it.

alternativesConsidered.name: Require an administrator for everyone
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A standard user on a Mac that already has Apple's tools needs no administrator; only one without them is refused, with the way on.

alternativesConsidered.name: A transaction that rolls every step back
alternativesConsidered.summary: Undo the whole set-up on any failure.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Steps such as Apple's tools and a browser sign-in cannot be rolled back cleanly; steps that check their own end state and run again on doubt resume or repair the one installation.

alternativesConsidered.name: Write the window into the owner's ~/.claude settings
alternativesConsidered.summary: Where the first plan put the 500k key.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Squire's session reads only its own config folder (ADR-003 line 3), so the key would never reach it.

alternativesConsidered.name: The environment variable as the only window route
alternativesConsidered.summary: Set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW in the runner and nothing in settings.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: One route already guarded by the runner's equality check and the digests is enough if the key reaches the session; measured, the key reaches the session, so the variable is not needed.

alternativesConsidered.name: Refuse to start the session on any doubt about the window
alternativesConsidered.summary: No session while a source cannot be read.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A managed file the owner cannot read would leave them with no Squire; the health check says it cannot confirm the window instead.

alternativesConsidered.name: Watch for Terminal by name
alternativesConsidered.summary: A deny-list of terminal apps for the no-Terminal check.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: It decides only the instances listed; the release check allows only the expected apps and fails anything else, and anything it cannot classify.

alternativesConsidered.name: The name and personality only in the Squire home, or a model-judged reply test
alternativesConsidered.summary: Other placements and proofs for the persona.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Kept in squire.json they stay the owner's; whether a reply uses a personality is a judgement, so the bound test reads what the session loads and the Journey test reads the first reply for the name.

alternativesConsidered.name: Back up somewhere other than iCloud Drive, or only the two listed cases
alternativesConsidered.summary: Other destinations or a narrower backup.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: iCloud Drive is what the owner approved; a backup that silently does nothing when iCloud is off, or overwrites a changed file, breaks the promise without a sign.

alternativesConsidered.name: A yes per piece, or a separate sign-in-again app
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The story asks for one yes for what will be installed; running the same app again resumes at the sign-in, so no second app is needed.

alternativesConsidered.name: Read managed settings through the Mac's preference commands
alternativesConsidered.summary: Have the health check shell out to defaults or plutil for the managed sources so a fake on PATH could answer.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: It would add commands only for the tests' sake; one root for the system places is smaller and is listed for the owner.

title: The set-up app: one download carrying core, steps that check their own end state, the plan checked by declaration and by sign-in, and the settings, persona, backup and known fixes it lays down
